newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - May 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - May 19.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Monday:
KINSHASA - Thousands of reinforcements streamed into Kinshasa to consolidate the control of Laurent Kabila's insurgent movement, while government troops surrendered their weapons.

KIGOMA, TANZANIA - Friends of Zaire's victorious rebel Laurent Kabila describe him as a principled man of strong character but the Bembe people of eastern Zaire say he is a traitor, a killer and a thief.

WASHINGTON - Two of the nation's largest public universities are reporting a substantial decline in the number of minorities they are admitting in the first classes after the schools were barred from using race as a factor in picking students.
WASHINGTON - Recent efforts to improve academic standards have led to a new age of untimed tests.
WASHINGTON - Washington, D.C. Police Chief Larry Soulsby, bolstered by the support of the city's financial control board, is working to rebuild his image and the city police department.

WASHINGTON - Democratic National Committee officials have abandoned hope of eliminating the party's huge financial debt by the end of the year and have been forced to consider cutting programs and planned staff growth.
